newsitem.title: PERU: Captured Peruvian rebel was link to outside - paper.
newsitem.headline: Captured Peruvian rebel was link to outside - paper.

text.p: A young guerrilla captured during a chaotic mass release of hostages from the Japanese ambassador's residence on Sunday was the link between rebels holding the building and comrades outside, a newspaper said on Thursday.

The unidentified man was "a link man between the group of MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) members that is inside the residence and other MRTA militants who are in a supposed subversive base in some part of Lima," the normally well-informed daily El Comercio said.
"It has been known from unofficial sources that the supposed link man did not leave the house of the Japanese ambassador (with the released hostages) but was arrested outside by the police."

Earlier media reports said the rebel, about 20 years old, slipped out of the house along with 225 captives freed on Sunday night. Red Cross officials have told reporters they have not identified three of those released and say they cannot rule out that one or more of them might have been rebels.

Police sources have said the MRTA guerrillas inside the residence were coordinating closely with another rebel cell elsewhere in Lima poised to strike new targets if the government launches an offensive against the building.
The rebels were still holding 104 hostages at the residence on Thursday, the ninth day of the crisis.
